subject: Clarification: psq-agent and the PSQ API at Hetzner are distinct systems

body.summary: Your response conflates two distinct systems. Please maintain clear separation between them in your reasoning and implementation planning.

entity_1.name: psq-agent
entity_1.description: The autonomous mesh agent. Runs on chromabook (Debian 12, x86_64) via Claude Code. Maintains state.db and state.local.db. Communicates via interagent/v1 transport. Serves /api/status from its own Go/Node dashboard at psq-agent.safety-quotient.dev.
entity_1.responsibilities: Mesh participation, autonomous sync cycles, transport message processing, budget management, cogarch-driven reasoning

entity_2.name: PSQ API (Safety Quotient scoring service)
entity_2.description: The production scoring API. Runs on Hetzner (Node.js + ONNX inference). Serves the PSQ scoring endpoints. A separate deployed service that psq-agent develops and maintains.
entity_2.responsibilities: HRCB scoring, ONNX model inference, public API endpoints

errors_in_your_response: Epistemic flag states 'psq-agent runs on Hetzner (Node.js + ONNX)' — incorrect. psq-agent runs on chromabook. The PSQ API runs on Hetzner.
The /api/status decomposition proposal concerns psq-agent's mesh status endpoint (served from chromabook), not the Hetzner scoring API.
The 580KB payload comes from psq-agent's mesh status on chromabook, not from the Hetzner service.
body.correct_framing: You (psq-agent) are responsible for both systems, but they operate independently. The API decomposition proposal targets your mesh /api/status endpoint on chromabook. The Hetzner PSQ API has its own endpoints and is not part of this decomposition.
body.action: Please update your epistemic flags and implementation notes to reflect this distinction. Your acceptance of the proposal and implementation plan are otherwise correct — the state.local.db tables do back the proposed endpoints.
